rules.problem: Page gives a cluster ('Thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60, dehydration likely'); the rule makes any single item sufficient, so thirst alone, dry mouth alone or diastolic < 60 alone gives probable dehydration and, through active_condition Dehydration, an Urgent priority. This over-calls a 'likely' diagnosis.

rules.rule: Urgent: weakness or tiredness with red-box findings
rules.problem: The red-box criterion 'Hb < 6 →44' is missing entirely, so a tired patient with Hb 5 is not flagged Urgent. Also, the fever criterion drops the 'in past 3 days' window. The remaining items, the and/or structure, the trigger and the Urgent level are faithful to the box heading.
The page says 'Check Hb. If < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely' (p43-9b35877c), so the house standard calls for a probable Anemia rule. No such rule exists.

summary: Most serious: the red-box criterion 'Hb < 6' is missing from the Urgent priority rule, and there is no Hb measure task. The page's 'anaemia likely' (Hb < 12 woman / < 13 man) has no probable diagnosis rule. The dehydration rule makes any single sign (thirst, dry mouth, poor turgor, SBP < 90 or DBP < 60) enough for probable dehydration and so Urgent, and the fever criterion drops the 3-day window. Every other cited condition faithfully matches the page.
